writeup: TIC 295124562 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse with 18.82% dimming and a secondary eclipse detected at 9.8 sigma significance. The BLS periodogram signal reaches 418.4 signal-to-noise ratio, with pixel-level analysis confirming the signal at 40.9 sigma in difference imaging. However, a significant data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ notably in depth, suggesting the true orbital period is approximately 41.09 days rather than the 20.55 days initially measured. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. While pixel-level confirmation supports the reality of the signal, the alternating eclipse-depth pattern remains an open question requiring further investigation.
